source.snippet: Twelve real experiments, eight hours, zero landed. The bug was in the instrument, not the robot. [Post about building an automated job application bot and the challenge of measuring whether it actually works]

problem_statement: Job seekers and developers building automated job application tools have no reliable way to measure whether their automation is actually working — the feedback loop (callbacks, rejections) is too slow and noisy to debug the system.
target_segment: Tech-savvy job seekers, career coaches, and indie developers building job search automation tools
notes: Builder invested 8 hours in an experiment — real time cost. Recurring pain: anyone building or using job application automation faces the same measurement gap. A lightweight observability/testing harness for job application bots could be a paid SaaS or API. The dev.to post had 14 score and 6 comments suggesting community resonance.
